key_insight: Multilingual multimodal machine learning can distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic primary progressive aphasia with high accuracy in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals using connected speech.
clinical_relevance: This could speed up and support differential diagnosis in bilingual patients, where traditional language assessment is time-intensive and harder to deliver consistently.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients completed a picture-description task in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Researchers extracted speech-timing, word-level, linguistic, and image-text congruence features from recordings.
Classification models and ensemble methods were compared across languages; performance was tested with McNemar analysis.
evidence_signal: The best model achieved macro F1 scores of 93% with word-level features and 92% with an ensemble, with no significant performance difference between dominant and non-dominant language samples.
watch_item: The study is small and language-specific, so broader validation is needed before use in routine clinical workflows.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
